title: Paul Graham on startup ideas, founders, and making things people want (Moonshots clips)
summary: Podcast hosts discuss Paul Graham using clips of him speaking. He argues good ideas come from side projects rather than brainstorming, that expertise in users beats startup mechanics, that founders matter more than ideas, and that doing things manually and iterating quickly with users beats polish.

principles.text: Don't brainstorm startup ideas; build a mind and life that produces them unconsciously, often as side projects.
principles.quote: the way to get startup ideas is not to try to think of startup ideas

principles.text: Succeeding requires deep expertise in your users, not expertise in how startups work.
principles.quote: What you need to know to succeed in a startup is not expertise in startups what you need is expertise in your own users

principles.text: Going through the motions of a startup (funding, office, hires) neglects the only essential thing: making something people want.
principles.quote: they have neglected the one thing that's actually essential which is to make something people want

principles.text: At the earliest stage, the founders matter far more than the idea.
principles.quote: the founder is more important than the idea a lot more important

principles.text: Do things manually for early customers; it is worth the unscalable work because you learn a lot.
principles.quote: it's so important to get early customers that if you have to do a ton of manual stuff that's okay you'll learn a lot from it

principles.text: Ship a rough first version fast and iterate through many rounds of user conversations.
principles.quote: as long as you get it out there very quickly it doesn't matter as if it's if it's not great because you start the conversation with users
